passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: In addition to the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K (this Annual Report) and the exhibits hereto, the following risk factors should be considered carefully in evaluating our business. Our business, financial condition, cash flows or results of operations could be materially adversely affected by any of these risks. This section contains forward-looking statements. You should refer to the explanation of the qualifications and limitations on forward-looking statements set forth at the end of Part I, Item 1. Business of this Annual Report. The considerations and risks that follow are organized within relevant headings but may be relevant to other headings as well. Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also adversely affect our business, financial condition, cash flows or results of operations. Economic, Industry and Geopolitical Risks We face intense competition and may not be able to keep pace with the rapid technological changes in the medical devices industry or low-cost competitive offerings, which could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition or results of operations. The medical device markets in which we participate are highly competitive. We encounter significant competition across our product lines and in each market in which our products are sold from various medical device companies. Some of our competitors may have greater financial and marketing resources than we do, including as a result of consolidation among companies in our industry. Our primary competitors include large manufacturers with multiple lines of business and competing products, as well as a wide range of medical device companies that sell a single or limited number of competitive products or which participate in only a specific market segment or segments. We also face competition from non-medical device companies, including pharmaceutical companies, biotech companies and providers of various diagnostic solutions, which may offer alternative therapies for disease states also amenable to diagnosis or treatment using our products. New competitors may emerge in the future, potentially including companies introducing new sales or distribution models to our industry or leveraging genomic, robotic, navigation, and/or other automation technologies. Digital technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning capabilities, have and may continue to increase in their applicability and importance to various aspects of our business, operating and competitive environments, research and development (R&D) pipeline and product portfolio. We believe we will need to develop new and enhanced digital capabilities and competences in order to remain competitive. In addition, the medical device markets in which we participate are characterized by extensive research and development and rapid technological change. Developments by other companies of products and/or services, processes or technologies, including low-cost alternatives, may make our products or proposed products obsolete or less competitive and may negatively impact our net sales. It is necessary for us to devote

credit_strengths.text: Revenue and operating income have compounded at a double-digit pace over the disclosed trend, lifting the EBITDA proxy and keeping operating margin in line with the health care sector median. This scale and profitability support internal cash generation and provide a buffer against pricing or procedure-volume pressure in the electrophysiology and cardiovascular franchises.

Operating cash flow covers capital expenditure comfortably, leaving free cash flow that represents a solid share of interest-bearing debt. That conversion, combined with a current ratio above the sector median, indicates the balance sheet can fund working capital, research and development, and bolt-on acquisitions without incremental leverage.

key_risks.text: The debt note shows a large euro-denominated senior note stack maturing in the medium term, with the revolving facility extended to a later date. Refinancing this ladder at higher coupons would raise cash interest, and the disclosed ratings-linked coupon reset on the long-dated note adds sensitivity to any future rating action.

The risk-factor passage flags intense competition and rapid technological change in medical devices, including low-cost alternatives and digital or AI-enabled entrants. Because growth is concentrated in electrophysiology and a single pulsed-field ablation platform, any share loss or reimbursement shift there would pressure revenue and the EBITDA proxy that underpins leverage.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is well above the sector median, and free cash flow to debt sits comfortably above the median, so cash earnings cover fixed charges with a wide cushion. Net leverage is modest and sits below the sector median on a cash-netted basis, leaving headroom before the next threshold.

The maturity profile is manageable, with no single year's scheduled amortisation overwhelming annual free cash flow, and the undrawn revolver provides backup liquidity. Our judgement is that the issuer can refinance maturities and absorb modest EBITDA volatility without breaching the indicative leverage threshold.

overall_credit_view.text: We view the credit as solidly investment-grade in character, supported by scale, double-digit organic growth, and cash conversion that funds capital expenditure and acquisitions. The indicative financial risk profile is modest, with leverage below the sector median and cash-flow coverage above it, though the profile is not a rating.

Forward-looking, we expect leverage to remain near current levels absent a large debt-funded acquisition, given the disclosed acquisition spend and the absence of dividend or buyback data in the bundle. Competitive and technological risk in electrophysiology is the main watch item, and we would monitor coupon resets on refinancing.

credit_strengths.text: 於披露趨勢期內，收入及經營收入以雙位數步伐複合增長，推高 EBITDA proxy，並使經營利潤率與醫療保健行業中位數保持一致。此規模及盈利能力支持內部現金生成，並為電生理及心血管業務面對定價或手術量壓力提供緩衝。
經營現金流從容覆蓋資本開支，留下自由現金流，佔計息債務一個穩健份額。該轉換，加上流動比率高於行業中位數，表明資產負債表可為營運資金、研發及補強型收購提供資金，而無需增加槓桿。

key_risks.text: 債務票據顯示一個大型歐元計值優先票據組合於中期到期，而循環融資則延長至較後日期。以較高票息為此到期階梯再融資將提高現金利息，而長年期票據所披露與評級掛鈎的票息重置，增加對任何未來評級行動的敏感度。
風險因素章節指出醫療器械行業競爭激烈及技術快速變化，包括低成本替代品及數碼或 AI 賦能的新進入者。由於增長集中於電生理及單一脈衝場消融平台，該領域任何份額流失或報銷轉變將對收入及支撐槓桿的 EBITDA proxy 構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率遠高於行業中位數，而自由現金流對債務比率亦穩居中位數之上，因此現金盈利以寬裕緩衝覆蓋固定費用。淨槓桿溫和，並以現金淨額基準計低於行業中位數，在下一門檻前留有空間。
到期結構可控，並無任何單一年度的計劃攤銷壓倒年度自由現金流，而未提取的循環融資提供備用流動性。我們判斷發行人可為到期債務再融資，並吸收溫和的 EBITDA 波動，而不會違反指示性槓桿門檻。

overall_credit_view.text: 我們認為該信用在特徵上穩健地屬於投資級，受規模、雙位數內生增長及現金轉換支持，而現金轉換為資本開支及收購提供資金。指示性財務風險狀況溫和，槓桿低於行業中位數，而現金流覆蓋高於中位數，儘管該狀況並非評級。
前瞻而言，我們預期在沒有大型債務融資收購的情況下，槓桿將維持於接近當前水平，鑑於所披露的收購開支及資料包中並無股息或回購數據。電生理領域的競爭及技術風險為主要觀察事項，而我們將監測再融資時的票息重置。
